To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the comonomer incorporation into a growing polymer chain is strongly enhanced by the coordination of its functional groups to the active site in the polymerization of butadiene with styrene- and aniline-functionalized dienes.
functionalized monomers can be copolymerized in a highly efficient and controlled manner with a nonfunctionalized diene, e.g., butadiene.
the comonomer incorporation of functionalized 1,3-dienes in butadiene copolymerization with [(mesitylene)-Ni(allyl)]+ is enhanced by coordination of the functional group of the comonomers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new catalyst systems for the synthesis of functionalized polybutadienes by copolymerization of butadiene with monomer functionalized dienes.
the development of novel functional polymers with well-defined structures and the investigation of their properties and potential applications in, e.g, catalysis, materials science, and biomedicine.
the development of novel, highly efficient catalysts for the polymerization of conjugated dienes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functional group coordination is a key factor for the comonomer incorporation and the overall polymerization rate.
comonomer functional groups can be used in a synergetic manner to increase the reactivity of a monomer with the growing chain end, and thus, to enhance the comonomer incorporation.
the comonomer incorporation is not just a consequence of a favorable binding of comonomer to Ni-1, but rather the combination of a favorable binding with a favorable comonomer insertion rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the monomer functional group coordination is a powerful tool for controlling comonomer incorporation and stereoregularity in copolymerizations of functionalized dienes with butadiene.

monomer coordination in catalytic insertion polymerization can be used to enhance comonomer incorporation, to control the comonomer sequence, and, in the case of polar comonomers, to control the microstructure of the resulting copolymer.
the functional group coordination is a general phenomenon for the catalytic insertion copolymerization of dienes with PhS-functionalized dienes, which can be extended to other functional groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the functional group can act as an additional coordination site for the monomer, thus increasing the comonomer incorporation and the overall reaction rate.
the functional group of comonomers may be exploited in catalytic insertion polymerizations to enhance their incorporation and thus to tailor copolymer properties.
comonomer reactivities in catalytic insertion polymerizations can be controlled by tuning the binding strength of the monomer to the active site.
